001package io.jstach.rainbowgum;
002
003import java.net.URI;
004import java.util.ArrayList;
005import java.util.List;
006import java.util.Locale;
007import java.util.Map;
008import java.util.NoSuchElementException;
009import java.util.Optional;
010import java.util.Set;
011import java.util.function.Function;

015
016import io.jstach.rainbowgum.annotation.CaseChanging;
017
018/**
019 * Describes a key (or several fallback keys) resolved against a {@link LogProperties}
020 * instance - start with {@link LogProperties#forKey(String)} - and also serves as the
021 * namespace for the shared property machinery: {@link Result}, {@link Validator}, and the
022 * property-specific exceptions.
023 *
024 * @see LogProperties
025 */
026@CaseChanging
027public interface LogProperty {
028
029        /**
030         * The first key tried.
031         * @return key.
032         */
033        public String key();
034
035        /**
036         * Every key tried, in order - the first key given to
037         * {@link LogProperties#forKey(String)}/{@link LogProperties#forKey(String, String)}
038         * followed by any added via {@link #or(String)}/{@link #or(String, String)}.
039         * @return keys.
040         */
041        public List<String> keys();
042
043        /**
044         * The properties this key (or keys) will be looked up against.
045         * @return properties.
046         */
047        public LogProperties properties();
048
049        /**
050         * Resolves the property as a raw string.
051         * @return result.
052         */
053        public Result<String> ofString();
054
055        /**
056         * Resolves the property as a list, using {@link LogProperties#listOrNull(String)}.
057         * @return result.
058         */
059        public Result<List<String>> ofList();
060
061        /**
062         * Resolves the property as a map, using {@link LogProperties#mapOrNull(String)}.
063         * @return result.
064         */
065        public Result<Map<String, String>> ofMap();
066
067        /**
068         * Resolves the property as an int.
069         * @return result.
070         */
071        default Result<Integer> ofInt() {
072                return ofString().map(Integer::parseInt);
073        }
074
075        /**
076         * Resolves the property as a boolean.
077         * @return result.
078         */
079        default Result<Boolean> ofBoolean() {
080                return ofString().map(Boolean::parseBoolean);
081        }
082
083        /**
084         * Resolves the property as a URI.
085         * @return result.
086         */
087        default Result<URI> ofURI() {
088                return ofString().map(URI::new);
089        }
090
091        /**
092         * Resolves the property as a {@link LogProviderRef} for component provision.
093         * @return result.
094         * @see LogOutput#of(LogProviderRef)
095         */
096        default Result<LogProviderRef> ofProviderRef() {
097                return switch (ofURI()) {
098                        case Result.Success<URI> s -> mapValue(s, LogProviderRef.of(s.value(), s.key()));
099                        case Result.Missing<URI> m -> m.convert();
100                        case Result.Error<URI> e -> e.convert();
101                };
102        }
103
104        /**
105         * Resolves the property as a {@link LogProviderRef} and then maps it to a
106         * {@link LogProvider}.
107         * @param <U> provider type.
108         * @param mapper function to map to provider.
109         * @return result.
110         * @see LogOutput#of(LogProviderRef)
111         */
112        default <U> Result<LogProvider<U>> ofProvider(
113                        PropertyFunction<LogProviderRef, LogProvider<U>, ? super Exception> mapper) {
114                return ofProviderRef().map(mapper);
115        }
116
117        /**
118         * Rewraps a value that was already derived from success's value, keeping the
119         * {@link PropertySuccess}'s origin (topProperties/properties/key/rawValue/kind)
120         * intact - useful for a conversion step that cannot itself throw, so
121         * {@link Result#map(PropertyFunction)} would be overkill, but that still needs to
122         * keep the result's origin intact for a later conversion step's error message.
123         * @param <T> success's value type.
124         * @param <U> new value type.
125         * @param success success to take the origin from.
126         * @param value already-converted value to wrap.
127         * @return new success of the same shape as success, wrapping value.
128         */
129        static <T, U> Result.Success<U> mapValue(Result.Success<T> success, U value) {
130                return switch (success) {
131                        case PropertySuccess<T> ps ->
132                                new PropertySuccess<>(ps.topProperties(), ps.properties(), ps.key(), ps.rawValue(), ps.kind(), value);
133                };
134        }
135
136        /**
137         * Builds a rich error from a failed conversion of a previously successful result -
138         * package-visible (rather than private) only so the top-level {@link PropertySuccess}
139         * can call it from {@link Result#map(PropertyFunction)}.
140         * @param <U> the converted value type.
141         * @param previousResult the success being converted.
142         * @param e the conversion failure.
143         * @return a rich error result.
144         */
145        static <U> Result.Error<U> richError(Result.Success<?> previousResult, Exception e) {
146                String fqk = previousResult.key();
147                PropertySuccess<?> ps = switch (previousResult) {
148                        case PropertySuccess<?> p -> p;
149                };
150                if (ps.kind() == PropertySuccess.Kind.VALUE) {
151                        String resolvedKey = ps.topProperties().description(fqk);
152                        String message = "Error for property. key: " + resolvedKey + ", " + e.getMessage();
153                        return new Result.Error<>(resolvedKey, message, e);
154                }
155                var badProps = ps.properties();
156                String resolvedKey = "'" + fqk + "' from " + badProps.description(fqk);
157                String message;
158                if (e instanceof PropertyConvertException || e instanceof ValidationException) {
159                        message = "Error converting property. key: " + resolvedKey + ", value: '" + ps.valueDescription()
160                                        + "' cause:\n" + e.getMessage();
161                }
162                else {
163                        message = "Error for property. key: " + resolvedKey + ", " + errorName(e) + " " + e.getMessage();
164                }
165                message += "\nTried: '" + fqk + "' from " + ps.topProperties().description(fqk);
166                return new Result.Error<>(resolvedKey, message, e);
167        }
168
169        /**
170         * Prefers {@link PropertyProblem#errorName()} (a short, stable name) over the
171         * exception's actual class name - a foreign exception (not one of ours) just gets its
172         * full class name as before.
173         */
174        private static String errorName(Exception e) {
175                if (e instanceof PropertyProblem pp) {
176                        return pp.errorName();
177                }
178                return e.getClass().getName();
179        }
180
181        /**
182         * Checks that value is not null, throwing {@link PropertyMissingException} naming key
183         * if it is. Useful for a property that is required but was set programmatically (e.g.
184         * a builder setter) rather than resolved through {@link #ofString()}/etc, so there is
185         * no {@link Result} to check for missing-ness.
186         * @param <T> value type.
187         * @param key property key, used only in the exception message.
188         * @param value value to check.
189         * @return value, never null.
190         * @throws PropertyMissingException if value is null.
191         */
192        static <T> T require(String key, @Nullable T value) {
193                if (value == null) {
194                        throw new PropertyMissingException("Value is required not null. property key='" + key + "'");
195                }
196                return value;
197        }
198
199        /**
200         * Adds a fallback key to try (without <code>{name}</code> interpolation) if none of
201         * the keys tried so far are found. Keys already added are tried first, in order; this
202         * one is tried last.
203         * @param fallbackKey additional key to try.
204         * @return a new LogProperty trying this key's keys followed by fallbackKey.
205         */
206        default LogProperty or(String fallbackKey) {
207                validateKey(fallbackKey);
208                return withKey(fallbackKey);
209        }
210
211        /**
212         * Adds a fallback key to try (with <code>{name}</code> interpolated to nameParam) if
213         * none of the keys tried so far are found.
214         * @param fallbackKey additional key to try, containing a <code>{name}</code>
215         * placeholder.
216         * @param nameParam value to interpolate for <code>{name}</code>.
217         * @return a new LogProperty trying this key's keys followed by fallbackKey.
218         */
219        default LogProperty or(String fallbackKey, String nameParam) {
220                String interpolated = LogProperties.interpolateNamedKey(fallbackKey, nameParam);
221                validateKey(interpolated);
222                return withKey(interpolated);
223        }
224
225        private LogProperty withKey(String fallbackKey) {
226                List<String> combined = new ArrayList<>(keys());
227                combined.add(fallbackKey);
228                return new DefaultLogProperty(List.copyOf(combined), properties());
229        }
230
231        /**
232         * Creates a LogProperty for a single key.
233         * @param properties properties this key will be looked up against.
234         * @param key key.
235         * @return LogProperty.
236         */
237        static LogProperty of(LogProperties properties, String key) {
238                validateKey(key);
239                return new DefaultLogProperty(List.of(key), properties);
240        }
241
242        /**
243         * Creates a LogProperty for a single key with a <code>{name}</code> parameter
244         * interpolated.
245         * @param properties properties this key will be looked up against.
246         * @param key key, containing a <code>{name}</code> placeholder.
247         * @param nameParam value to interpolate for <code>{name}</code>.
248         * @return LogProperty.
249         */
250        static LogProperty of(LogProperties properties, String key, String nameParam) {
251                String interpolated = LogProperties.interpolateNamedKey(key, nameParam);
252                validateKey(interpolated);
253                return new DefaultLogProperty(List.of(interpolated), properties);
254        }
255
256        /**
257         * Validates a fully resolved (post <code>{name}</code> interpolation) property key -
258         * must start with {@value LogProperties#ROOT_PREFIX}, must not start or end with
259         * {@value LogProperties#SEP}, and must not use a reserved key parameter name.
260         * @param key fully resolved key to validate.
261         * @throws IllegalArgumentException if key is malformed.
262         */
263        private static void validateKey(String key) {
264                if (!key.startsWith(LogProperties.ROOT_PREFIX)) {
265                        throw new IllegalArgumentException(
266                                        "Property key should start with: '" + LogProperties.ROOT_PREFIX + "'. key = " + key);
267                }
268                if (key.endsWith(LogProperties.SEP) || key.startsWith(LogProperties.SEP)) {
269                        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Property key should not start or end with '" + LogProperties.SEP + "'");
270                }
271                LogProperties.validateKeyParameters(key, Set.of());
272        }
273
274        /**
275         * An error friendly {@link Function} for converting properties.
276         *
277         * @param <T> input type.
278         * @param <R> output type.
279         * @param <E> error type.
280         */
281        public interface PropertyFunction<T extends @Nullable Object, R extends @Nullable Object, E extends Exception>
282                        extends Function<T, R> {
283
284                @Override
285                default R apply(T t) {
286                        try {
287                                return _apply(t);
288                        }
289                        catch (Exception e) {
290                                sneakyThrow(e);
291                                throw new RuntimeException(e);
292                        }
293                }
294
295                /**
296                 * Apply that throws error.
297                 * @param t input
298                 * @return output
299                 * @throws E if an error happened in function.
300                 */
301                public R _apply(T t) throws E;
302
303                @SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
304                private static <E extends Throwable> void sneakyThrow(final Throwable x) throws E {
305                        throw (E) x;
306                }
307
308        }
309
310        /**
311         * Parent interface for property exceptions.
312         */
313        sealed interface PropertyProblem permits PropertyConvertException, PropertyMissingException, ValidationException,
314                        LogProviderRef.NotFoundException {
315
316                /**
317                 * A short, stable name for this problem used in error messages instead of the
318                 * exception's full (and for a nested class, {@code $}-separated) class name.
319                 * Deliberately hardcoded per implementation rather than derived via
320                 * {@code getClass().getSimpleName()} so it stays stable across renames/moves of
321                 * the actual exception class.
322                 * @return error name.
323                 */
324                String errorName();
325
326        }
327
328        /**
329         * Property helper mixin.
330         */
331        interface PropertySupport {
332
333                /**
334                 * String key value properties.
335                 * @return properties.
336                 */
337                public LogProperties properties();
338
339        }
340
341        /**
342         * Thrown if an error happens while converting a property.
343         */
344        final static class PropertyConvertException extends RuntimeException implements PropertyProblem {
345
346                private static final long serialVersionUID = -6260241455268426342L;
347
348                /**
349                 * Key.
350                 */
351                private final String key;
352
353                /**
354                 * Creates convert exception.
355                 * @param key property key.
356                 * @param message error message
357                 * @param cause maybe null.
358                 */
359                PropertyConvertException(String key, String message, @Nullable Throwable cause) {
360                        super(message, cause);
361                        this.key = key;
362                }
363
364                /**
365                 * Property key.
366                 * @return key.
367                 */
368                public String key() {
369                        return this.key;
370                }
371
372                @Override
373                public String errorName() {
374                        return "PropertyConvertException";
375                }
376
377        }
378
379        /**
380         * Throw if property is missing.
381         */
382        final static class PropertyMissingException extends NoSuchElementException implements PropertyProblem {
383
384                private static final long serialVersionUID = 4203076848052565692L;
385
386                /**
387                 * Creates a missing property exception.
388                 * @param s error message.
389                 */
390                PropertyMissingException(String s) {
391                        super(s);
392                }
393
394                @Override
395                public String errorName() {
396                        return "PropertyMissingException";
397                }
398
399        }
400
401        /**
402         * Thrown by {@link Validator#validate()} when one or more of the accumulated
403         * {@link Result}s failed, reporting every failure in a single message instead of just
404         * the first one encountered.
405         */
406        final static class ValidationException extends RuntimeException implements PropertyProblem {
407
408                private static final long serialVersionUID = -8416817560218813225L;
409
410                ValidationException(String message, @Nullable Throwable cause) {
411                        super(message, cause);
412                }
413
414                @Override
415                public String errorName() {
416                        return "ValidationException";
417                }
418
419                /**
420                 * Validates a list of results and throws {@link ValidationException} if any
421                 * results are not {@link Result.Success}.
422                 * @param builder class to prefix to full message.
423                 * @param results list of results.
424                 * @throws ValidationException if any result in the supplied list is not
425                 * successful.
426                 */
427                public static void validate(Class<?> builder, List<Result<?>> results) throws ValidationException {
428                        StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder().append("Validation failed for ")
429                                .append(builder.getName())
430                                .append(":");
431                        Throwable cause = null;
432                        boolean failed = false;
433                        for (var r : results) {
434                                switch (r) {
435                                        case Result.Success<?> s -> {
436                                                continue;
437                                        }
438                                        case Result.Missing<?> m -> {
439                                                sb.append("\n");
440                                                sb.append(m.message());
441                                                failed = true;
442                                        }
443                                        case Result.Error<?> e -> {
444                                                sb.append("\n");
445                                                sb.append(e.message());
446                                                if (cause == null) {
447                                                        cause = e.cause();
448                                                }
449                                                failed = true;
450                                        }
451                                }
452                        }
453                        if (failed) {
454                                throw new ValidationException(sb.toString(), cause);
455                        }
456
457                }
458
459                /**
460                 * Wraps cause in a {@link ValidationException}, using the same "Validation failed
461                 * for &lt;class&gt;:" message prefix {@link #validate(Class, List)} itself uses.
462                 * {@link ValidationException}'s constructor is package-private, so this is the
463                 * supported way for code outside this package - generated builder code in
464                 * particular - to report a downstream factory method's own defensive/cross-field
465                 * check (an {@link IllegalArgumentException}, say) through the same channel as a
466                 * per-field validation failure, without duplicating the message format itself.
467                 * Returns rather than throws so the caller writes
468                 * {@code throw ValidationException.of(...)} - keeps the throw itself, and
469                 * therefore unreachable-code/definite-assignment analysis at the call site,
470                 * visible there instead of hidden inside this method.
471                 * @param builder class to prefix to the message, same role as
472                 * {@link #validate(Class, List)}'s own parameter.
473                 * @param cause the exception to wrap.
474                 * @return a new {@link ValidationException} wrapping cause; not thrown by this
475                 * method.
476                 */
477                public static ValidationException of(Class<?> builder, RuntimeException cause) {
478                        return new ValidationException("Validation failed for " + builder.getName() + ": " + cause.getMessage(),
479                                        cause);
480                }
481
482        }
483
484        /**
485         * Accumulates {@link Result}s from one or more property lookups and validates them
486         * together, so that a caller resolving several properties in sequence can report
487         * every failure at once instead of failing fast on the first bad property.
488         * <p>
489         * This is the mechanism generated {@code fromProperties(LogProperties)} builder
490         * implementations use: each property is looked up and its {@link Result} is added to
491         * the validator as it is read; {@link #validate()} is then called once at the end,
492         * after all properties have been read, so a user who misconfigured several properties
493         * sees all of the problems together rather than fixing them one at a time across
494         * repeated runs.
495         * <p>
496         * Use {@link #add(Result)} for a property that is required: a {@link Result.Missing}
497         * is treated as a failure. Use {@link #addIfError(Result)} for an optional property
498         * that already has a fallback applied (typically via {@link Result#or(Object)} with
499         * the builder's current field value): a {@link Result.Missing} is expected in that
500         * case and is silently ignored, but a {@link Result.Error} (the property was present
501         * but failed to convert) is still a real problem and is reported.
502         *
503         * @apiNote a {@code Validator} is single-use: create one with {@link #of(Class)}, add
504         * every result that should be checked, and call {@link #validate()} exactly once at
505         * the end.
506         */
507        public static class Validator {
508
509                private final List<Result<?>> results = new ArrayList<>();
510
511                private final Class<?> builder;
512
513                /**
514                 * Creates a validator whose {@link ValidationException} messages will be prefixed
515                 * with the name of the given class.
516                 * @param builder the class on whose behalf properties are being resolved -
517                 * typically the builder calling this method. It is only used to identify the
518                 * source of a failure in the exception message; no state is read from it.
519                 * @return newly created validator.
520                 */
521                public static Validator of(Class<?> builder) {
522                        return new Validator(builder);
523                }
524
525                private Validator(Class<?> builder) {
526                        this.builder = builder;
527                }
528
529                /**
530                 * Adds a result that must be present. Both {@link Result.Missing} and
531                 * {@link Result.Error} will cause {@link #validate()} to fail. Use this for a
532                 * required property; for an optional property that already has a fallback value
533                 * applied, use {@link #addIfError(Result)} instead so a missing value does not
534                 * itself trigger a failure.
535                 * @param result result to check.
536                 * @return this.
537                 */
538                public Validator add(Result<?> result) {
539                        results.add(result);
540                        return this;
541                }
542
543                /**
544                 * Adds a result only if it is a {@link Result.Error}; a {@link Result.Missing}
545                 * result is silently ignored. Intended for an optional property that has already
546                 * had a fallback value applied (for example via {@link Result#or(Object)}): the
547                 * property being absent is expected and fine, but if it was present and failed to
548                 * convert that should not be swallowed.
549                 * @param result result to check.
550                 * @return this.
551                 */
552                public Validator addIfError(Result<?> result) {
553                        if (result instanceof Result.Error<?> e) {
554                                results.add(e);
555                        }
556                        return this;
557                }
558
559                /**
560                 * Validates every result added so far via {@link #add(Result)} or
561                 * {@link #addIfError(Result)}, throwing a single exception listing all failures
562                 * if one or more of them are not {@link Result.Success}.
563                 * @throws ValidationException if any added result is a {@link Result.Missing}
564                 * (added via {@link #add(Result)}) or a {@link Result.Error} (added via either
565                 * method).
566                 */
567                public void validate() throws ValidationException {
568                        ValidationException.validate(builder, results);
569                }
570
571        }
572
573        /**
574         * The result of a property fetched from properties.
575         *
576         * @param <T> property type.
577         */
578        sealed interface Result<T> {
579
580                /**
581                 * Registers this result with {@code validator} via {@link Validator#add(Result)}
582                 * (a still-{@link Missing} result is treated as a real failure) and returns this
583                 * result unchanged, so a chain that builds a required property can register
584                 * itself with a shared {@link Validator} and keep going in one expression -
585                 * {@code properties.forKey(key).ofString().or(fallback).validate(v)} - instead of
586                 * a separate {@code var x = ...; v.add(x);} statement pair. The validator is
587                 * shared and single-use by design: add every property's result this way (or via
588                 * {@link #validateIfError(Validator)} for an optional one), then call
589                 * {@link Validator#validate()} exactly once at the end to report every failure
590                 * together instead of one exception per property.
591                 * @param validator validator to add this result to.
592                 * @return this result, unchanged.
593                 */
594                default ValidatedResult<T> validate(Validator validator) {
595                        validator.add(this);
596                        return (ValidatedResult<T>) this;
597                }
598
599                /**
600                 * Like {@link #validate(Validator)} but via {@link Validator#addIfError(Result)}
601                 * instead of {@link Validator#add(Result)} - a {@link Missing} result is expected
602                 * and ignored, only a {@link Result.Error} is treated as a failure. Intended for
603                 * an optional property that already has a fallback applied (for example via
604                 * {@link #or(Object)}): the property being absent is fine, but if it was present
605                 * and failed to convert that should not be swallowed.
606                 * @param validator validator to add this result to.
607                 * @return this result, unchanged.
608                 */
609                default ValidatedResult<T> validateIfError(Validator validator) {
610                        validator.addIfError(this);
611                        return (ValidatedResult<T>) this;
612                }
613
614                /**
615                 * Convenience for a genuine one-off, single-property validation that does not
616                 * need to participate in a larger batch: builds a single-use {@link Validator},
617                 * registers this result with it via {@link Validator#add(Result)}, and validates
618                 * immediately - instead of registering with a caller-managed {@link Validator}
619                 * via {@link #validate(Validator)} and deferring to a later
620                 * {@link Validator#validate()} call.
621                 * <p>
622                 * Uses {@link Validator#add(Result)} semantics: a still-{@link Missing} result is
623                 * treated as a failure, same as an absent required property with no fallback. If
624                 * this property is optional, apply a fallback first -
625                 * {@code properties.forKey(key).ofString().or(fallback).validateNow(component)} -
626                 * since a result with a fallback applied is never {@link Missing}. For a property
627                 * that should tolerate being missing but not being present-and-malformed, use
628                 * {@link #validateIfError(Validator)} with an externally-owned {@link Validator}
629                 * instead - there is deliberately no addIfError-equivalent of this method, to
630                 * avoid two same-named single-property convenience methods with silently
631                 * different failure semantics.
632                 * @param component the class on whose behalf this property is being resolved -
633                 * only used to name the source of the failure in the exception message.
634                 * @return value.
635                 * @throws ValidationException if this result is not a {@link Success}.
636                 */
637                default T validateNow(Class<?> component) {
638                        var v = Validator.of(component);
639                        v.add(this);
640                        v.validate();
641                        var result = switch (this) {
642                                case ValidatedResult<T> vr -> vr;
643                        };
644                        return result.value();
645                }
646
647                /**
648                 * Returns the current result if fallback is null or returns fallback as a result
649                 * if this result is missing.
650                 * @param fallback maybe <code>null</code>.
651                 * @return value.
652                 */
653                public Result<T> or(@Nullable T fallback);
654
655                /**
656                 * Returns the current result if success or error otherwise fallback supplier is
657                 * used. If the supplier returns <code>null</code> then the result will be mising.
658                 * @param fallback may return <code>null</code> but not recommended.
659                 * @return value.
660                 */
661                public Result<T> or(Supplier<T> fallback);
662
663                /**
664                 * Maps this result's value through {@code mapper}. On success, keeps the origin
665                 * ({@link PropertySuccess#topProperties() topProperties}/properties/key/
666                 * rawValue/kind, see {@link PropertySuccess}) so a later conversion step's error
667                 * message can still point back to it. On failure, builds a rich error message -
668                 * which key it came from, where that key was found, and (for
669                 * {@link PropertyConvertException}/{@link ValidationException} causes) the
670                 * original raw value - with a "Tried:" line searching {@code topProperties}: the
671                 * {@link LogProperties} the very first {@link LogProperties#forKey(String)} in
672                 * this chain was looked up against, which for a chained/composite
673                 * {@code LogProperties.of(a, b)} can be broader than the exact source the value
674                 * was actually found at. Usable at any point in a chain, not just directly off a
675                 * {@link LogProperty}, since a {@link Success} keeps pointing back to the
676                 * property it originally came from no matter how many conversions have run since.
677                 * @param <U> result type
678                 * @param mapper mapping function.
679                 * @return mapped result.
680                 */
681                public <U> Result<U> map(PropertyFunction<T, U, ? super Exception> mapper);
682
683                /**
684                 * A description of the result for error messages.
685                 * @return description.
686                 */
687                public String describe();
688
689                /**
690                 * A property that is present.
691                 *
692                 * @param <T> property type.
693                 */
694                public sealed interface Success<T> extends RequiredResult<T> permits PropertySuccess {
695
696                        @Override
697                        default @Nullable T valueOrNull() {
698                                return value();
699                        }
700
701                        /**
702                         * Gets the value and will never fail for Success.
703                         * @return value.
704                         */
705                        @Override
706                        public T value();
707
708                        @Override
709                        default Success<T> or(@Nullable T fallback) {
710                                return this;
711                        }
712
713                        @Override
714                        default Success<T> or(Supplier<T> fallback) {
715                                return this;
716                        }
717
718                        /**
719                         * Original property key where the value was derived from or was passed a
720                         * fallback.
721                         * @return key.
722                         */
723                        public String key();
724
725                }
726
727                /**
728                 * A property that is missing (<code>null</code>).
729                 *
730                 * @param <T> property type.
731                 * @param properties the properties that were searched, kept around so
732                 * {@link #or(Object)} can hand it to the {@link PropertySuccess} it builds for a
733                 * supplied fallback.
734                 * @param keys keys.
735                 * @param message description of where the property is missing.
736                 */
737                public record Missing<T>(LogProperties properties, List<String> keys,
738                                String message) implements ValidatedResult<T> {
739                        /**
740                         * A property that is missing (<code>null</code>).
741                         * @param properties the properties that were searched.
742                         * @param keys keys.
743                         * @param message description of where the property is missing.
744                         */
745                        public Missing {
746                                if (keys.isEmpty()) {
747                                        throw new IllegalArgumentException("one key is required");
748                                }
749                        }
750
751                        @Override
752                        public @Nullable T valueOrNull() {
753                                return null;
754                        }
755
756                        @Override
757                        public T value() throws NoSuchElementException {
758                                throw new PropertyMissingException(message);
759                        }
760
761                        @Override
762                        public Result<T> or(@Nullable T fallback) {
763                                if (fallback != null) {
764                                        return new PropertySuccess<>(properties, properties, keys.get(0), fallback,
765                                                        PropertySuccess.Kind.VALUE, fallback);
766                                }
767                                return this;
768                        }
769
770                        @Override
771                        public Result<T> or(Supplier<T> fallback) {
772                                return or(fallback.get());
773                        }
774
775                        /**
776                         * Helper just to cast the result to a different parameterized type.
777                         * @param <R> parameterized type.
778                         * @return this.
779                         */
780                        @SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
781                        public <R> Missing<R> convert() {
782                                return (Missing<R>) this;
783                        }
784
785                        @Override
786                        public <U> Missing<U> map(PropertyFunction<T, U, ? super Exception> mapper) {
787                                return convert();
788                        }
789
790                        @Override
791                        public String describe() {
792                                return "Missing[" + keys + "]";
793                        }
794
795                }
796
797                /**
798                 * A property that was present but failed conversion.
799                 *
800                 * @param <T> property type.
801                 * @param key property key that failed to convert.
802                 * @param message failure message.
803                 * @param cause exception thrown while trying to convert.
804                 */
805                @SuppressWarnings("JavaLangClash")
806                public record Error<T>(String key, String message, Exception cause) implements ValidatedResult<T> {
807                        /*
808                         * TODO consider rename to Failure
809                         */
810                        @Override
811                        public @Nullable T valueOrNull() {
812                                throw new PropertyConvertException(key, message, cause);
813                        }
814
815                        @Override
816                        public T value() throws PropertyConvertException {
817                                throw new PropertyConvertException(key, message, cause);
818                        }
819
820                        @Override
821                        public Error<T> or(@Nullable T fallback) {
822                                return this;
823                        }
824
825                        @Override
826                        public Error<T> or(Supplier<T> fallback) {
827                                return this;
828                        }
829
830                        /**
831                         * Helper just to cast the result to a different parameterized type.
832                         * @param <R> parameterized type.
833                         * @return this.
834                         */
835                        @SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
836                        public <R> Error<R> convert() {
837                                return (Error<R>) this;
838                        }
839
840                        @Override
841                        public <U> Error<U> map(PropertyFunction<T, U, ? super Exception> mapper) {
842                                return convert();
843                        }
844
845                        @Override
846                        public String describe() {
847                                return "Error[" + key + "](" + message + ")";
848                        }
849                }
850
851        }
852
853        /**
854         * A {@link Result} that is safe to pull a value out of - either because it can never
855         * actually be missing ({@link RequiredResult}: a {@link Success} or an
856         * {@link Result.Error}, both already resolved one way or the other) or because a
857         * caller has explicitly acknowledged the possibility of a still-{@link Missing}
858         * result by running it through {@link Result#validate(Validator)},
859         * {@link Result#validateIfError(Validator)}, or {@link Result#validateNow(Class)}.
860         * <p>
861         * {@link Result} itself deliberately does not declare {@link #value()}/
862         * {@link #valueOrNull()}/{@link #optional()} - a bare {@link Result} returned by
863         * {@link LogProperty#ofString()} and friends forces a caller through one of those
864         * validation paths before it can pull a value out, instead of blindly calling
865         * {@code value()} on a result that might still be {@link Missing}.
866         *
867         * @param <T> property type.
868         */
869        sealed interface ValidatedResult<T> extends Result<T> {
870
871                /**
872                 * Gets the value and will fail with {@link NoSuchElementException} if there is no
873                 * value.
874                 * @return value.
875                 * @throws PropertyMissingException if there is no value.
876                 * @throws PropertyConvertException if the property failed conversion.
877                 */
878                public T value() throws PropertyMissingException, PropertyConvertException;
879
880                /**
881                 * Gets the value.
882                 * @return value or <code>null</code>.
883                 */
884                public @Nullable T valueOrNull();
885
886                /**
887                 * Gets a value if there is if not uses the fallback.
888                 * @param fallback maybe <code>null</code>.
889                 * @return value.
890                 */
891                default @Nullable T valueOrNull(@Nullable T fallback) {
892                        var v = valueOrNull();
893                        if (v != null) {
894                                return v;
895                        }
896                        return fallback;
897                }
898
899                /**
900                 * Convenience that turns a value into an optional.
901                 * @return optional.
902                 */
903                default Optional<T> optional() {
904                        return Optional.ofNullable(valueOrNull());
905                }
906
907        }
908
909        /**
910         * A result that is not missing and will either be an error or success.
911         *
912         * @param <T> property type.
913         */
914        sealed interface RequiredResult<T> extends ValidatedResult<T> {
915
916        }
917
918}
919
920/**
921 * A property that is present, either because it was actually found in properties, or
922 * (when {@code kind} is {@link Kind#VALUE}) because it was missing there and a fallback
923 * value was supplied instead.
924 * <p>
925 * Not public: nothing outside {@code LogProperty}'s own resolution machinery (in this
926 * package) constructs or pattern-matches on this directly - callers work through the
927 * sealed {@link LogProperty.Result}/{@link LogProperty.Result.Success} interfaces
928 * instead.
929 *
930 * @param <T> property type.
931 * @param topProperties the {@link LogProperties} the very first
932 * {@link LogProperties#forKey(String)} in this chain was looked up against - for a
933 * chained/composite {@code LogProperties.of(a, b)} this is the whole composite, not just
934 * whichever member the value ended up found in. Used for a failure message's "Tried:"
935 * line, which can therefore search more broadly than {@code properties}.
936 * @param properties the properties searched; for {@link Kind#STRING}/{@link Kind#LIST}/
937 * {@link Kind#MAP} the <strong>exact</strong> properties where the value was found - for
938 * a chained/composite search this can be narrower than {@code topProperties}, naming just
939 * the one member the value was actually found in. Used for a failure message's "key: ...
940 * from X" line.
941 * @param key property key.
942 * @param rawValue value as originally found (or the fallback, for {@link Kind#VALUE}),
943 * before any conversion - a {@link String}, {@link List List&lt;String&gt;}, or
944 * {@link Map Map&lt;String,String&gt;} depending on kind.
945 * @param kind which of {@link LogProperty}'s {@code ofString()}/{@code ofList()}/
946 * {@code ofMap()} this property was found through, and so rawValue's runtime type - or
947 * {@link Kind#VALUE} if it was not found at all and rawValue is a fallback.
948 * @param value actual (possibly converted) value.
949 * @apiNote rawValue/kind stick around after a conversion (e.g.
950 * {@link LogProperty#ofInt()} converting the string this was found as into an
951 * {@code Integer}) so error messages can still describe the original value - value's type
952 * and rawValue's kind are not always in sync.
953 */
954record PropertySuccess<T>(LogProperties topProperties, LogProperties properties, String key, Object rawValue,
955                PropertySuccess.Kind kind, T value) implements LogProperty.Result.Success<T> {
956
957        /**
958         * Which of {@link LogProperty}'s typed accessors a {@link PropertySuccess} was found
959         * through, and so what {@link PropertySuccess#rawValue()}'s runtime type actually is
960         * - or that it was not found at all and is a plain fallback value.
961         */
962        enum Kind {
963
964                /**
965                 * rawValue is a {@link String}, found via {@link LogProperty#ofString()}.
966                 */
967                STRING,
968                /**
969                 * rawValue is a {@link List List&lt;String&gt;}, found via
970                 * {@link LogProperty#ofList()}.
971                 */
972                LIST,
973                /**
974                 * rawValue is a {@link Map Map&lt;String,String&gt;}, found via
975                 * {@link LogProperty#ofMap()}.
976                 */
977                MAP,
978                /**
979                 * Not found in properties at all - rawValue is a plain fallback value supplied
980                 * via {@link LogProperty.Result#or}.
981                 */
982                VALUE
983
984        }
985
986        /**
987         * Successfully found property value.
988         * @param topProperties the properties the original lookup started from.
989         * @param properties the properties searched.
990         * @param key property key.
991         * @param rawValue value as originally found (or the fallback), before any conversion.
992         * @param kind rawValue's kind.
993         * @param value actual value should not be <code>null</code>.
994         */
995        PropertySuccess {
996                if (value == null) {
997                        throw new NullPointerException("value");
998                }
999        }
1000
1001        @Override
1002        public <U> LogProperty.Result<U> map(LogProperty.PropertyFunction<T, U, ? super Exception> mapper) {
1003                try {
1004                        U u = mapper._apply(value);
1005                        return new PropertySuccess<>(topProperties, properties, key, rawValue, kind, u);
1006                }
1007                catch (Exception e) {
1008                        return LogProperty.richError(this, e);
1009                }
1010        }
1011
1012        @Override
1013        public String describe() {
1014                if (kind == Kind.VALUE) {
1015                        return "Fallback[" + key + "]=" + value;
1016                }
1017                return "Property[" + key + "]=" + valueDescription();
1018        }
1019
1020        String valueDescription() {
1021                String s = kind == Kind.STRING ? (String) rawValue : String.valueOf(rawValue);
1022                return maybeRedact(s);
1023        }
1024
1025        private static final Set<String> REDACTED_KEYS = Set.of("password", "apikey", "secret", "token");
1026
1027        private static final String REDACTED_VALUE = "<REDACTED>";
1028
1029        private static String maybeRedact(String input) {
1030                String lower = input.toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT);
1031                if (REDACTED_KEYS.contains(lower)) {
1032                        return REDACTED_VALUE;
1033                }
1034                for (var k : REDACTED_KEYS) {
1035                        if (input.contains(k)) {
1036                                return REDACTED_VALUE;
1037                        }
1038                }
1039                return input;
1040        }
1041
1042}
1043
1044final class DefaultLogProperty implements LogProperty {
1045
1046        private final List<String> keys;
1047
1048        private final LogProperties properties;
1049
1050        DefaultLogProperty(List<String> keys, LogProperties properties) {
1051                super();
1052                if (keys.isEmpty()) {
1053                        throw new IllegalArgumentException("at least one key is required");
1054                }
1055                this.keys = keys;
1056                this.properties = properties;
1057        }
1058
1059        @Override
1060        public String key() {
1061                return keys.get(0);
1062        }
1063
1064        @Override
1065        public List<String> keys() {
1066                return keys;
1067        }
1068
1069        @Override
1070        public LogProperties properties() {
1071                return this.properties;
1072        }
1073
1074        @Override
1075        public Result<String> ofString() {
1076                return resolve(k -> properties.visit(k, (p, kk) -> {
1077                        var v = p.valueOrNull(kk);
1078                        return v == null ? null : new PropertySuccess<>(properties, p, kk, v, PropertySuccess.Kind.STRING, v);
1079                }));
1080        }
1081
1082        @Override
1083        public Result<List<String>> ofList() {
1084                return resolve(k -> properties.visit(k, (p, kk) -> {
1085                        var v = p.listOrNull(kk);
1086                        return v == null ? null : new PropertySuccess<>(properties, p, kk, v, PropertySuccess.Kind.LIST, v);
1087                }));
1088        }
1089
1090        @Override
1091        public Result<Map<String, String>> ofMap() {
1092                return resolve(k -> properties.visit(k, (p, kk) -> {
1093                        var v = p.mapOrNull(kk);
1094                        return v == null ? null : new PropertySuccess<>(properties, p, kk, v, PropertySuccess.Kind.MAP, v);
1095                }));
1096        }
1097
1098        private <T> Result<T> resolve(java.util.function.Function<String, Result.@Nullable Success<T>> lookup) {
1099                for (String k : keys) {
1100                        var success = lookup.apply(k);
1101                        if (success != null) {
1102                                return success;
1103                        }
1104                }
1105                return missingResult(properties, keys);
1106        }
1107
1108        <T> Result.Missing<T> missingResult(LogProperties props, List<String> keys) {
1109                List<String> resolvedKeys = describeKeys(props, keys);
1110                String message = "Property missing. keys: " + resolvedKeys;
1111                return new Result.Missing<>(props, keys, message);
1112        }
1113
1114        List<String> describeKeys(LogProperties props, List<String> keys) {
1115                return keys.stream().<String>map(k -> {
1116                        String fqk = fullyQualifiedKey(k);
1117                        return "'" + fqk + "' from " + props.description(fullyQualifiedKey(k));
1118                }).toList();
1119        }
1120
1121        String fullyQualifiedKey(String key) {
1122                return key;
1123        }
1124
1125}
